jobs.title: Product Manager, Documentation Systems
jobs.description: About Versapay 🚀 Versapay turns accounts receivable (AR) into a competitive advantage. Inefficient AR processes slow cash flow and stall growth. Versapay removes friction, unlocks working capital, and accelerates momentum — giving finance leaders the clarity and control they need to drive business forward. Versapay automates accounts receivable, removing barriers to collecting and reconciling B2B payments. Our solutions connect finance teams, customers, and business systems in one ecosystem to ensure cash flow clarity. With over 10,000 customers and 5M+ companies transacting on the platform, Versapay processes over 110M transactions and $257B annually. Think you might be the next Veep to join? Read on!! How you’ll make an impact here – and on your career: Product management at Versapay is a craft that blends strategic thinking, customer empathy, and strong execution. As Product Manager, Documentation Systems, you will own our documentation as a product: the in-product Help our customers rely on, the implementation and support knowledge our internal teams run on, and the systems that produce both. This is a build role. Our AI tooling can draft a help article. It cannot tell us whether that article is true, decide whether it should exist, or get an engineer to explain what shipped. You will own the pipeline that produces our documentation, the standards it runs on, and the judgment calls it cannot make. You will sit on the Product Management team as a peer to the product managers who own our platform and our embedded ERP applications. You will have modern LLM tooling, fully sanctioned and connected to our internal systems, and a mandate to build on it. What you’ll do: Own the Documentation Surface Own our full documentation surface: in-product Help, implementation guides, support runbooks, and release notes, across our platform and our embedded applications. Decide what gets documented, what gets rewritten, and what gets retired. Build an information architecture prioritized by what customers search for and get stuck on, rather than by what shipped most recently. Define and own the metrics: documentation shipped with the release, page freshness, Help searches returning no results, and support volume on topics we believed were covered. Build the Documentation Pipeline Design and build an AI-assisted pipeline that drafts documentation from our real sources of truth: tickets, pull requests, release artifacts, and recorded demos. Build the evaluation process that catches the pipeline producing convincing but incorrect content before a customer does. Automate change detection, terminology and style enforcement, screenshot capture, and publishing. Own the toolchain. We author in MadCap Flare today and publish into a repo that our product loads. You will decide what to keep, what to automate around, and what to change. Improve How We Capture Product Knowledge Our tickets today describe what we set out to build, not what we shipped, so documenting a feature currently means reverse engineering it. Change that. Partner with Product and Engineering to establish a definition of done that captures how a feature works: navigation, permissions, configuration, error states, and impact on existing users. Build the terminology and style standards that let both people and models write consistently across four ERP surfaces where the same concept carries four different names. Keep Documentation True ERPs change their interfaces on their own schedule, and our documentation goes stale when they do. Design the detection and revalidation process and own the SLA on it. Learn our products by using them, working out how they behave rather than reading specifications describing how they were intended to. Write the small share of content that requires a person: migration guides, error taxonomies, and integration behaviour, where being wrong costs a customer their month-end close. What you’ll bring to the team: Required Qualifications 5+ years own

jobs.title: Product Owner, Xsolla Partner Network
jobs.description: About You We are looking for a Product Owner to join the team behind Xsolla Partner Network (XPN). The role is based in the US, and we’re open to strong candidates globally. Partner Network connects game publishers with content creators to drive discovery, engagement, and revenue. XPN is a two-sided marketplace. We help publishers run creator marketing campaigns (xsolla.com/partner-network), and we give creators a way to join those campaigns, along with tools to manage and grow their channels (xsolla.com/for/creators). Each side has its own users and goals, and each shapes the other. Helping both sides succeed together is what makes this role so interesting. You’ll work closely with customers on both sides and with a collaborative team that’s building something new in the creator economy. You’ll bring what you learn back to the Product Director and the team, help shape where the product goes, and then work alongside design and engineering to bring it to life. This is a hands-on role that mixes customer conversations, product definition, and day-to-day delivery. If you enjoy turning what you learn from customers into shipped features, and you like doing it with a team that moves fast and supports each other, we’d love to meet you. About Us Xsolla is a global commerce company with robust tools and services to help developers solve the inherent challenges of the video game industry. From indie to AAA, companies partner with Xsolla to help them fund, distribute, market, and monetize their games. Grounded in the belief in the future of video games, Xsolla is resolute in the mission to bring opportunities together, and continually make new resources available to creators. Headquartered and incorporated in Los Angeles, California, Xsolla operates as the merchant of record and has helped over 1,500+ game developers to reach more players and grow their businesses around the world. With more paths to profits and ways to win, developers have all the things needed to enjoy the game. For more information, visit xsolla.com. Responsibilities: Research and discovery. Get to know both sides of the XPN marketplace: the game publishers running creator campaigns and the creators bringing those campaigns to life. Talk with customers, gather insights, and keep up with trends in the creator economy and gaming. What you learn shapes where the product goes next. Coordinate the roadmap. Work with the Product Director to turn insights into priorities. Bring ideas and recommendations, balance publisher and creator needs, and help build a roadmap the whole team is excited about. Write product requirements. Turn ideas into clear, well-scoped PRDs that give design and engineering what they need to build with confidence. Manage delivery. Organize the work in Jira and keep design, engineering, and QA aligned and moving from kickoff through release. Track what matters. Define and follow the metrics that show how XPN is working for publishers and creators, and use them to guide what we build next. Keep everyone connected. Be the hub for product communication. Share project status, research, and customer insights with the product team. Keep Business Development, Customer Success, and Marketing up to date on what’s shipping and what it means for our partners. Requirements: Product experience. 3+ years in product management or product ownership, shipping software alongside a dedicated engineering team. Customer insight. You enjoy talking with customers and turning those conversations into insights that shape product decisions. You’re comfortable serving more than one type of user and finding solutions that work for everyone involved. Clear writing. You write product requirements that are easy to follow and help the team get aligned quickly. Engineering partnership. You work closely with engineers day to day, making scope and sequencing decisions together, and you’re comfortable managing the backlog and tracking work

Workato unifies data, applications, and processes into a single platform so AI can reliably orchestrate business processes in production at enterprise scale. Built on more than a decade of running mission-critical processes for over half the Fortune 500 — including Nasdaq, Amazon, Cisco, Vodafone, Atlassian, and Lucid Motors — Workato turns over 14,000 enterprise systems AI needs to act on into one governed execution layer. For more information, visit workato.com. Why join us? Ultimately, Workato believes in fostering a flexible, trust-oriented culture that empowers everyone to take full ownership of their roles . We are driven by innovation and looking for team players who want to actively build our company. But, we also believe in balancing productivity with self-care . That’s why we offer all of our employees a vibrant and dynamic work environment along with a multitude of benefits they can enjoy inside and outside of their work lives. If this sounds right up your alley, please submit an application. We look forward to getting to know you! This is a one-year internship with intent to hire, and a rare opportunity to own a high-visibility project from day one and directly shape how the team defines, plans, and delivers agentic use cases. You won’t just be analyzing requirements; you’ll uncover patterns in how functional work moves through our system, run the agile cadence that gets it delivered, and turn what you learn into solutions the Technical Owner and Functional Lead will act on. In this role, you will also be responsible to: Program Management Responsibilities You will own the operating rhythm that keeps Packaged Genies’ delivery predictable and visible: Agile Cadence Ownership: Run the day-to-day agile cadence across all workstreams; sprint planning, backlog grooming, standups, and retrospectives — not just observing them, but running them. Jira Story Preparation: Based on direction from the Technical Owner, decompose requirements into well-structured Jira epics and stories with clear descriptions, acceptance criteria, and dependencies, so the team has sufficient clarity to execute. Milestone & Deliverable Tracking: Set and track milestones for the requirement-to-delivery pipeline (requirement → breakdown → task → done), flagging slippage early and keeping the Technical Owner informed with concise, accurate status updates. Stakeholder Alignment: Align stakeholders across workstreams; Product Owner, Technical Lead, Functional Lead, and engineering; on scope, sequencing, and dependencies. Program Documentation: Document your approach, decisions, and findings in Confluence so the program’s knowledge stays accessible and current. Analytical & Functional Responsibilities Alongside program management, you will do the structured groundwork that helps leadership make informed delivery and process decisions: Requirements Gathering: Partner with workstream leads across Packaged Genies to gather functional requirements and turn them into structured, usable specs. Pattern Analysis: Classify and categorize functional requirements and use cases to surface patterns; recurring integration types, common breakdown gaps, sizing errors and build a process to keep this current. jobs.description: ABOUT RAMP Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books. The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving. We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome. The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same. If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it. ABOUT THE ROLE You will build and run the operating systems that help Juno ship reliably and support customers as we scale. On the product operations side, you will turn product decisions into clear operating plans, maintain visibility in Linear, coordinate customer testing and launch readiness, keep commitments and risks visible, and make sure product changes are communicated clearly. You will partner closely with product and engineering to make decisions executable, keep work organized, surface gaps and dependencies, and ensure the team follows through on what it has committed to ship. On the customer support side, you will be the first line of defense when customers encounter product issues. You will triage and investigate problems, coordinate the right response, and redirect travel-service questions to our travel partners. Because you sit close to both the product process and the customer, you will turn recurring friction into clear insights, accountable follow-up, and better operating systems. Success means Juno ships through a lightweight and dependable process, customers understand what changed, risks and commitments do not get lost, recurring issues reach the right owners, and support demand does not grow one-for-one with the business. WHAT YOU’LL DO - Provide holistic support through the entire launch lifecycle across program management, customer testing, launch readiness, change management, customer communication, and post-launch iteration. Own and improve Juno's shipping process so the right reviews, testing, documentation, internal enablement, and customer updates happen at the right time. - Maintain Linear as a reliable operating system for projects, owners, milestones, dependencies, status, and product decisions. Surface risks early and follow through until they are resolved. - Serve as the first line of defense for product-related customer issues across email and chat, join customer calls when needed, manage escalations to resolution, and route travel-service questions to the right partner. - Be the voice of the customer in product decisions. Analyze support trends and customer feedback, diagnose recurring friction, size the problems you find, and translate messy input into clear findings, recommended actions, prioritization input, and accountable follow-up for product and engineering. - Build AI-powered workflows, automations, knowledge systems, and self-service experiences that improve the quality and speed of product operations and customer support. WHAT YOU NEED - 3+ years of experience in product operations, program management, customer experience, technical support, consulting, or another customer-facing analytical role in a fast-moving software company. - You are highly process-oriented. jobs.description: Hi! I'm [Shriya](https://www.linkedin.com/in/shriya-baddula-4b0b41386), and I lead QA at Ashby. We're hiring a QA Engineer to help us test and strengthen the quality of our product. I think of QA as something you build into the system, not as something you layer on top for added confidence. I'm not interested in gatekeeping quality or creating a process for its own sake. I care about feedback that's fast and useful, the kind engineers trust, and catching the problems users would actually notice. That's what brought me to Ashby. Engineers take on a lot of ownership, including the quality of their work, which often means they test it themselves. QA here isn't about convincing people to care or taking quality off their plate. It's about being another set of eyes on a fast-evolving product. Sometimes that means seeing the edge case. Sometimes that means spotting the product's blind spot before it hits production. In this role, you'll decide what to test, when to test, and which product areas are worth automating. We're a small team, so the work is mixed. We all roll up our sleeves when needed. **Most of your time, roughly 70%, is hands-on manual testing.** You'll work with engineers and other stakeholders on features as they ship, reproduce bugs reported by customers, and, for larger launches, coordinate testing across an entire feature area. The other 30% is automation. You'll write Playwright end-to-end tests and help expand test coverage. You do not need to be an SDET, and you do not need to have built a framework from scratch. **You do need to be comfortable writing code**, reading someone else's code, and getting better at both. If you've written some E2E tests and want to write more, that's the right starting point. We have an existing Playwright suite and page object structure you'll build on, and SDETs who will pair with you and help you grow. What Ashby gives you in return is the best of both early and growth-stage environments. The agency and no-nonsense of a seed startup: you decide what to test, work directly with the people building it, and operate in an almost-no-meeting culture. The product-market fit and scale of a growth-stage startup: 100,000+ weekly active users who depend on our software, which means the things you catch actually matter. We have notable customers like Notion, Linear, Shopify, and Snowflake. Our growth and retention metrics are best-in-class among our peers: we have tens of millions in ARR, growing >100% year over year, very low churn, and many years of runway. We’ll share more details once we meet. ### **Why You Should or Shouldn’t Apply** - You have strong product instincts. You test like a user and know the difference between "it works" and "it works the way someone would actually use it." - You're good at reproducing bugs. When something is broken, you narrow it down. You don't file vague bugs and move on. - You are self-sufficient and can scope your own work. Given a feature and a spec, you decide what's worth testing and what’s not, and you know when to ask for help when something is taking too long. - You want to grow on the automation side. You don't need to be an expert to be interested. You want to write more tests, get faster at it, and learn from the engineers around you. - You write clearly. Your writing should be concise, clear, and easy to follow. ### **Put Another Way, You Shouldn't Apply If** - You think of QA as gatekeeping. We don't have sign-off gates, and we're not adding them. Your influence comes from the quality of your judgment, not from a checkbox. - You're happiest when someone hands you a test plan and a set of instructions. This role operates on ownership, with you often deciding what to test and why. - You want to stay at the surface. Testing Ashby well means understanding it well. We are modernizing the 50 billion dollar plus animal health industry by giving veterinary organizations the tools to focus more on patient care. Backed by Y Combinator and top venture investors in Silicon Valley, New York and Miami, Vetcove is a fast-growing, mission-driven company. We are searching for talented and passionate people who want to help shape the future of veterinary care. You’ll sit at the intersection of product, engineering, design, and customer-facing teams — helping translate user feedback into actionable insights, supporting product launches, and ensuring our processes scale as we grow. This is an ideal role for someone who is eager to develop deep operational expertise and grow within a fast-moving, mission-driven company. Synthesize User Feedback: Collect and organize qualitative feedback from clinics, pet parents, and internal stakeholders, and surface patterns and themes to inform product decisions. Track & Report on KPIs: Monitor product performance dashboards, flag anomalies, and compile regular reports to help product managers stay on top of key metrics. Coordinate Cross-Functional Workflows: Help manage sprint planning logistics, backlog grooming, and cross-team communication to keep initiatives on track. Support QA Processes: Assist with quality assurance testing, document bugs and edge cases, and help define acceptance criteria alongside product and engineering teams. What We’re Looking For Bachelors Degree 1+ years of experience in product operations, business operations, project coordination, or a related role Strong written and verbal communication skills with exceptional attention to detail Comfort working with data, including experience with spreadsheets, dashboards, or basic analytics tools Highly organized with the ability to juggle multiple workstreams and deadlines in a fast-paced environment Curiosity about technology and a desire to understand how software products are built and used Bonus: exposure to SaaS products, healthcare or veterinary tech, or customer-facing roles The typical base pay range for this role across the U.S. is: $70,000/year -$110,000/year + bonus + equity + benefits. The range reflects the base hourly rate or annual compensation (as applicable), and does not include bonus, equity or other incentives.
